calls.reason: Nature shows negative headlines attract clicks, and Pew documents workplace AI anxiety. Neither links that anxiety or engagement incentives to the spread of this particular job-loss story.

Mail Online reported roughly halved click-through rates with AI summaries, even at the same ranking. Pew's browsing study and DCN's publisher referral declines reinforce the picture, although total attributable losses remain uncertain.

The Copilot experiment supports speed gains, while Abnormal describes shipping AI-assisted work after review. Neither resolves whether the benefiting engineers would reject production use or merely require oversight.

Anthropic's Advolve account claims smaller teams perform the same operations, but lacks verified staffing and quality details. Tidio reports substantial automation while retaining workers, leaving actual replacement capability unclear.

FutureSearch documents recurring failures alongside successful research and reliable performance on easy tasks. That mixed evidence cannot settle the broad, undefined assertion that deep research does not work.

BBC documents faulty Apple summaries that were suspended; Pew finds mixed but often useful experiences with search summaries. These do not establish broadly worsening usability across everyday products.
